# Summary of the Green Party Manifesto 2024

The Green Party's 2024 manifesto presents a vision for a "fairer, greener country" during what it describes as an ongoing cost-of-living crisis and climate emergency. The party argues that climate action and addressing inequality are interconnected solutions.

## Healthcare and Social Care
The manifesto proposes significant NHS investment, including £28 billion additional annual expenditure by 2030 and £20 billion in capital spending over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing rapid GP access, ensuring universal NHS dentist availability, boosting staff pay, and restoring public health budgets. The party pledges to protect the NHS from privatisation and introduce free personal social care, investing £20 billion annually in care services.

## Housing
The Greens commit to building 150,000 new social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering local authorities to introduce rent controls, and ending no-fault evictions. A "Fairer, Greener Homes Guarantee" would invest £29 billion over five years to insulate homes and £9 billion for heat pump installations.

## Energy and Climate
The manifesto calls for wind power to provide 70% of UK electricity by 2030, ending new oil and gas licences, and phasing out fossil fuel subsidies. The party supports community energy ownership and opposes nuclear power development. A carbon tax starting at £120 per tonne would fund the green transition.

## Economy and Work
Proposed economic measures include £40 billion average annual green investment, bringing privatised utilities (railways, water, energy) into public ownership, and introducing a wealth tax on assets above £10 million. Workers' rights would be strengthened through repealing anti-union legislation, introducing a £15 minimum wage, and pursuing maximum 10:1 pay ratios.

## Welfare and Education
The party proposes increasing Universal Credit by £40 weekly, abolishing the two-child benefit cap, and scrapping tuition fees while restoring maintenance grants. Education investment includes £8 billion for schools and moving academies into local authority control.

## Environment and Nature
Commitments include a Rights of Nature Act, protecting 30% of land and seas by 2030, returning water companies to public ownership, and introducing a Right to Roam Act for England.

## Democracy and Rights
The manifesto advocates proportional representation, votes at 16, defending human rights legislation, and replacing the House of Lords with an elected chamber.

## International Affairs
On foreign policy, the Greens call for an immediate ceasefire in Gaza, recognition of Palestine, ending UK arms exports to Israel, rejoining the EU, and signing the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons while cancelling Trident.
